paper_title: Thermal management of the hotspots in 3-D integrated circuits

scenario.figure_or_table: Table 1 (PDF page 3); Figure 4 (PDF page 4); Figure 6 (PDF page 4)
scenario.description: Two-die 3D-IC (die-1 10x10x5 mm, die-2 10x10x2 mm, 0.5 mm bonding layer) with a 1x1x1 mm hotspot in each die (6.0e9 W/m3 in die-1, 2.0e9 W/m3 in die-2). Compared: no cooling, interlayer micro-channel cooling (1.0 mm x 2.0 mm channel embedded in die-1 along x, water at 20 mg/s, 10 C inlet), and micro-channel plus a thermal TSV (600 W/mK) between the hotspot and the channel. Reported observable: temperature profile along y at x = 5.0 mm, z = 5.0 mm. Micro-channel cooling lowers temperature by about 70 K versus the uncooled case, with a further drop at the hotspot from the TTSV.
scenario.architecture: Two-die face-to-back 3D-IC with a bonding layer, bottom convective boundary (h = 1000 W/m2K, ambient 25 C), adiabatic top and side surfaces, and embedded micro-channel cooling with a TTSV
scenario.workload: Steady volumetric hotspot heat generation: 6.0e9 W/m3 in die-1 and 2.0e9 W/m3 in die-2 (1 mm3 each); no power time series
scenario.operating_point: Water coolant mass flow 20 mg/s, inlet 10 C, bottom heat transfer coefficient 1000 W/m2K, ambient 25 C

original_setup.solver: Not named. The paper gives a compact finite-volume-style heat conduction model (eq. 1, solids) with a convection term for the coolant (eq. 2), following the 3D-ICE formulation it cites. No code, mesh, or solver software is identified.
original_setup.optimizer: None. The paper compares three fixed cases (no cooling, micro-channel, micro-channel plus TTSV) and runs no optimization or placement search.
original_setup.controller: None. There is no dynamic thermal management or flow controller. The coolant mass flow is fixed at 20 mg/s.
original_setup.benchmark: Two-die face-to-back 3D-IC (die-1 10x10x5 mm, die-2 10x10x2 mm, 0.5 mm bonding layer) with a 1x1x1 mm hotspot in each die (6.0e9 W/m3 in die-1, 2.0e9 W/m3 in die-2). The paper compares three cases: no micro-channel or TTSV, micro-channel cooling, and micro-channel plus TTSV. The case is custom and has no named public benchmark.

thermal_observable.location: Temperature profile along the y-direction at x = 5.0 mm, z = 5.0 mm, compared between Fig. 5 (no cooling) and Fig. 6 (micro-channel cooling).
thermal_observable.aggregation: Text-reported temperature decrease of about 70 K from micro-channel cooling, read from a line profile. The paper does not state whether this is a peak, mean, or other value. Absolute temperatures and the extra TTSV reduction at the hotspot appear only in figures and are not quantified in the text.

physical_mismatches.reason: The model is a true 3D stack with two active dies, a bonding layer, and a vertical z axis with hotspots at different heights. A 2D single-layer floorplan thermal model cannot represent this vertical heat flow.

Interlayer micro-channel liquid cooling (1.0 x 2.0 mm channel along x, water at 20 mg/s, 10 C inlet) is central to the result. It adds a convective term (eq. 2) and coolant temperature rise that a conduction-only package/heat-sink model does not include.

The thermal TSV (600 W/mK, 1x1x1 mm) between the hotspot and the channel is a key mechanism. It is modeled via an effective conductivity (eq. 3) in a localized 3D volume and has no 2D floorplan analogue.
The heat sources are volumetric 1 mm3 hotspots specified in W/m3 at fixed 3D positions, not block-level watts on a chip floorplan. The workload has no multi-block layout and no power trace.

The boundary conditions are specific: bottom convection h = 1000 W/m2K at 25 C ambient, and adiabatic top and side surfaces. These differ from a typical Studio package stack with a heat sink and spreader.
The paper has no optimizer or controller. The study is a fixed-configuration steady comparison, so there is no placement optimizer or control policy to replicate.

Eq. 1 and eq. 2 include a transient term, but the reported results are temperature profiles for what appears to be a steady state. The paper does not state this explicitly, and no transient or time-series result is given.
The paper does not report reliability, hotspot-lifetime, or electromigration analysis. Only temperature profiles are given.

studio_assumptions: The packet does not describe the bundled Studio package or material stack, so none can be cited here.
Any Studio run would be a separate illustrative 2D model with its own package and material assumptions and a generated placement. Those coordinates and powers are not paper-derived facts.
Studio temperatures must not be compared numerically to the paper's ~70 K micro-channel reduction or to its profiles, because of the 3D, micro-channel, and TTSV mismatches.
missing_inputs: No linked assets, repository, code, config files, or supplementary data are given in the packet (assets list empty; artifact search found no links).
Solver name, software, mesh or grid resolution, and convergence settings are not given.
Fig. 5 and Fig. 6 temperature values are not tabulated. Absolute peak temperatures and the TTSV-specific reduction would have to be digitized from figures, with uncertainty.
Block power in watts is not published. Only volumetric heat generation (W/m3) is given, with no published rule for converting it to a block power or a total chip power.
Die sizes in Table 1 are printed in m3 but described in the text as mm. The Table 1 bottom heat transfer coefficient unit is also printed as Wm-1K-1 while the text says W/m2K.
Micro-channel position in y and z, channel count and spacing, and the TTSV count and diameter are not fully specified. Only one TTSV location is given.
The Fig. 4 heat generation layout is shown only graphically, and the z-extent for die-2 is partly ambiguous.
The paper gives no power time series, no 2D placement, and no optimizer, controller, or reliability inputs.
